title: Protocol for Convolutional Neural Networks based Automated Cellular Cryo-Electron Tomograms Annotation
protocol: Make an empty folder and cd into that folder at the command-line.
Run e2projectmanager.py.
Click the **Workflow Mode** drop-down menu next to navigate to the TomoSeg panel.
Click **Import Tomogram Files** on the left panel.
On the right panel, click **Browse** next to import_files.
Select the tomogram you would like to segment in the browser window and click **Ok**.
If downsample/bin the tomogram before processing, write the shrink factor in appropriate box.
Make sure that the **import_tomos** and **tomoseg_auto** box is checked.
Click **Launch** and wait for pre-processing to finish.
Select **Box training references**.
Press browse, and select an imported tomogram.
Leave **boxsize** as -1.
Press Launch.
Select your tomograms in the Raw Data window.
Enter a suffix for the ROIs in the Output Suffix text box.
In Normalize Images, select None.
Press OK.
Navigate to the Segment training references interface in the project manager window.
For Particles, browse to the output ROIs you generated in the previous step.
Leave Output blank and keep segment checked.
Press Launch.
Identify regions in the tomogram that do not contain the feature of interest.
Press the Clear button in the e2boxer window to delete previous selections.
Select boxes in the tomogram that do not contain the feature of interest, ensuring a variety of different non-feature cellular structures, empty space, gold fiducials, and high-contrast carbon.
Write particle output using a different Output Suffix like "_bad".
Select the Build training set option in the project manager.
In particles_raw, select the "_good" file.
In particles_label, select the "_good_seg" file.
In boxes_negative, select the "_bad" file.
Leave trainset_output blank.
Press Launch to start building the training set.
The program will print "Done" when it has finished.
Train the neural network using the project manager.
Select the "_trainset" file for training.
Set the number of iterations as needed to balance quality and time.
Write the filename of the trained neural network output in the **netout** text box.
Press **Launch** to start the training process.
Monitor initial quick prints to ensure normal values are displayed.
Review "trainout_" followed by the netout file name for training results upon completion.
Zoom out so there are 3*N images displayed in each row.
For each three images, ensure the first one is the ROI from the tomogram.
Ensure the second image corresponds to the manual segmentation of the ROI.
Verify that the third image shows the neural network output for the same ROI after training.
Consider the neural network well trained if the third image matches the second image closely.
For negative particles, ensure both the second and third images are largely blank.
If the training result appears incorrect, revisit and check the positive and negative training sets.
Correct any errors in the positive or negative training sets to improve accuracy.
Continue training the neural network for a few rounds if the segmentation is suboptimal but not totally wrong.
Choose the previously trained network for continued training from the **Train the neural network** panel.
Set a smaller learning rate, typically around 0.001, in the continued training process.
Proceed to segment the whole tomogram once satisfied with the result and accuracy of the neural network output.
Open the **Apply the neural network** panel.
Choose the tomogram used to generate the boxes in the tomograms box.
Select the saved neural network file.
Set the output filename.
Adjust the number of threads option if needed.
Process the tomogram slices, considering memory consumption based on thread count and tomogram size.
After processing finishes, open the output file in a visualization software to view the segmentation.
